chunks: With this chain, from al-Husayn, from his father, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites Surah al-Samā' and al-Ṭāriq in his obligatory prayers will have prestige and position with Allah on the Day of Judgment, and he will be among the companions of the prophets and their companions in Paradise.

key_terms.بِسَّمَاءِ وَالطَّارِقِ: Al-Samā' and Al-Ṭāriq (two specific Surahs of the Quran)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Samā' and Al-Ṭāriq in obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, emphasizing the specific merit of reciting Surah al-Samā' and al-Ṭāriq within the obligatory (farā'iḍ) prayers. The hadith promises the reciter a unique 'status' (jah) and 'rank' (manzilah) before God, culminating in companionship with the prophets and their loyal companions in Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on consistent, high-quality recitation as a means of spiritual elevation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hussain from his father from al-Mu’ala b. Khunays from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

Whoever recites Surah Tariq in his obligatory prayer would enjoy great prestige and position before Allah on the Day of Judgment and he would be among the friends of the prophets and their companions in Paradise.
